query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Plasma nitriding of TC4 (Ti6Al4V) will form a thin, hard titanium nitride surface layer that boosts hardness and wear resistance without unduly altering the alloy’s beneficial bulk properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Unmodified α+β dual-phase TC4 alloy with relatively low surface hardness and poor friction and wear performance.
generation.intervention: Apply plasma nitriding under controlled conditions (specific temperature, time, and nitrogen pressure settings) to induce surface nitrogen diffusion.
generation.conditions: Performance tests under high-contact, extreme-service conditions where wear resistance is critical; processing conditions that retain a temperature below the threshold for altering the bulk microstructure.
generation.structural_mediator: Development of a superficial TiN layer combined with induced compressive residual stresses.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen diffuses into the TC4 surface during plasma nitriding, forming a thin TiN layer that increases surface hardness and reduces wear while leaving the underlying α+β microstructure (responsible for ductility and fatigue resistance) largely unaffected.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated TC4, the plasma-nitrided samples will exhibit a marked increase in surface hardness and reduced wear rate, yet maintain comparable bulk mechanical properties such as toughness and fatigue life.
generation.baseline: Characteristics of untreated TC4 measured by standard hardness, wear, and fatigue tests.
generation.boundary: The nitriding must be optimized to remain on the surface (maintaining a layer thickness that does not compromise ductility) and tested under typical extreme-service contact loads and temperatures that ensure layer stability.
generation.uncertainty: The exact nitriding parameters (temperature, time, nitrogen pressure) needed to achieve the ideal balance between improved wear resistance and preserved ductility are uncertain, and the influence of induced residual stresses on long-term fatigue behavior needs clarification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of TC4 alloy will undergo plasma nitriding under the predetermined conditions, while a control set remains unmodified. Conduct standardized evaluations including surface hardness (e.g., Vickers hardness), wear testing (e.g., pin-on-disk test), fatigue life tests, and microstructural analyses (XRD and SEM) to verify the presence and structure of the TiN layer.
measurements: Surface layer thickness and phase characterization (via XRD/SEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma-nitrided TC4 samples do not show statistically significant enhancements in surface hardness and wear resistance (e.g., improvements below a threshold of around 10% relative to the untreated alloy) or if they display a substantial degradation in key bulk properties (e.g., a greater than 10% reduction in fatigue life), then the hypothesis is falsified.
